subject: MAP: traffic replay window options & dedicated capacity sizing
messages:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jin Soo Park <jinsoo.park@cloudretail.io>, CloudRetail Ops <ops@cloudretail.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: traffic replay window options & dedicated capacity sizing

Thanks for the call this morning — quick recap and next steps so we keep momentum toward the MAP milestones and your targeted mid‑May close. Attached is a short MAP draft (v2) that captures the milestones we discussed. Please review and confirm owners/comments inline.

Key MAP milestone for engineering: traffic replay / peak QPS load test
- Objective: validate end-to-end latency and cost at 95th percentile for production-like traffic (session mux + auth flows)
- Target peak QPS (your ask on call): please confirm — we captured ~12k as a ballpark
- Proposed windows (please pick a preferred one or propose alternatives):
  1) May 4–5, 2026 (US West maintenance window)
  2) May 11–12, 2026 (preferred by product team for feature completeness)
- Dependencies: dedicated capacity reservation (GPU pool), whitelisted IP ranges, snapshot of production traffic (anonymized), and runbook owner for rollback
- Deliverables before window: traffic_replay_spec.yaml, capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx (attached), final runbook w/ success criteria

Asks from CloudRetail for this milestone: confirm which window works, final peak QPS figure, and whether you need an SLA-backed Dedicated pool for the run (if yes we’ll surface commercial terms). If you want, we can provision a temporary dedicated pool for the run but need a 5‑business‑day lead time.

I’m looping Rishi below to confirm capacity sizing and a short validation checklist. Once we lock the window I’ll update the MAP with owners and the target close date.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachments referenced: MAP_draft_CloudRetail_v2.pdf, traffic_replay_spec.yaml, capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx
From: Jin Soo Park <jinsoo.park@cloudretail.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: CloudRetail Ops <ops@cloudretail.io>
Date: Sun, 26 Apr 2026 18:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: traffic replay window options & dedicated capacity sizing

Thanks Michael — good summary. A couple of quick items from our side:

- Peak QPS: we believe 12k is accurate for peak storefront activity (we'll validate with telemetry and confirm by EOD Tuesday).
- Window preference: May 11–12 looks better for our release calendar (May 4–5 conflicts with a planned schema migration).
- Dedicated pool: we would like a dedicated pool for the replay if pricing works — need estimate of incremental cost and whether Redwood can guarantee isolated egress for compliance.

Can you also confirm run duration expectations (continuous replay for 4 hours at peak vs multi‑burst testing)? And do you need a dry‑run earlier?

-Jin Soo
VP, Engineering Operations
CloudRetail
jinsoo.park@cloudretail.io

Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: traffic replay window options & dedicated capacity sizing

Thanks Jin Soo — noted. Short answers and next steps below: 

- Peak QPS: we'll treat 12k as the target and plan tests that exercise 0.5x, 1x, and 1.5x peak to capture headroom.
- Run duration: recommend a 2‑hour sustained plateau at peak with a preceding 1.5 hour ramp and 30 minute cool down for rollback checks (total ~4 hours). We can add multiple bursts across the two‑day window if you want broader sampling.
- Dry run: yes — we recommend a 60‑minute dry run at 50% of peak three business days before the main window.
- Dedicated pool estimate: attached capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx shows a baseline reserved GPU pool to handle sustained 12k QPS and a 3x burst headroom option. High‑level: baseline reserved pool (NVIDIA H100 equi) + NVMe caching expected; final commercial quote to be issued by SalesOps after you confirm window.

Looping Rishi to validate the assumptions below and own the runbook: Rishi — can you confirm NVMe vs RAM cache sizing and whether the 3x headroom recommendation is realistic for this workload? Also note network whitelisting window needed (ops@cloudretail.io already on list).

If May 11–12 works, I’ll update the MAP draft with the milestone owner names, the dry‑run date (May 6), and the target close date for the deal (May 20).

Best,
Michael

Thanks — quick technical ack and owners list. I can own the runbook and capacity validation. High level:

- Capacity sizing: 12k peak with 3x burst headroom looks reasonable if we provision a dedicated pool sized at ~1.8x of sustained baseline and enable NVMe prefix caching for large context traffic. I'll validate exact GPU count in the attached workbook and confirm by EOD Wednesday.
- Runbook owners/responsibilities:
  • Rishi Malhotra (Redwood) — runbook lead, capacity validation, preflight checklist
  • Marissa Cole (Redwood) — rollout & monitoring dashboard owner, tracing hooks, alert thresholds
  • CloudRetail Ops — provide anonymized traffic snapshot, approve IP whitelist, sign off on dry run
- Canary plan: run first 60‑minute dry run at 50% peak on May 6 (Redwood to monitor qps/latency/cost and validate rollback)
- Final: Main replay May 11, start 08:00 PT, ramp to plateau over 90 minutes, 2 hour plateau, then cooldown; total window reserved until 14:00 PT.

I’ll upload a short runbook snippet into the shared Drive link and finish the capacity sheet (capacity_estimate_v1.xlsx). If CloudRetail needs an SLA-backed Dedicated pool we’ll coordinate SalesOps for terms (Michael — loop SalesOps after Jin confirms).

Rishi

Redwood Inference
